comments.body: 2026-11-07 re-triage: this card said nothing hands over a selection's bounds, which is wrong: ghostty_text_s has them at the pin and at vt-1.0.0. Retitled and moved out of uncommitted. It also proposed asking upstream, which the change-dependency practice rules out; a gap like this is closed by a small carried patch, and none is needed for the read.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`ghostty_surface_read_selection` hands over a selection's text, and Muster reads only that. `a_2Jrhh1dkA` therefore keeps the click count and re-drives two presses at the projected cell after a scroll. That works only because a press more than one cell width from the last resets libghostty's count, and it needs a rule about never landing twice on the same cell, or the word becomes a line.

The bounds are already in the same struct. `ghostty_text_s` carries `offset_start` and `offset_len`, which `Surface.dumpTextLocked` computes as `start = tl.y * cols + tl.x` and `end = br.y * cols + br.x`, so dividing by `cols` gives each corner's viewport cell. Renderer.swift:689 ignores those fields. This holds at the pin and at vt-1.0.0.

One limit: Surface.zig's comment says the offsets are wrong when the selection is partly outside the viewport. A word or line selection made by a click is in the viewport when it is made, which is when Muster needs it. Check a wrapped selection on a real surface first; not tested. No selection setter exists at vt-1.0.0, so the re-drive's second half, placing the selection again, still needs a look: this may only simplify it.
title: Read a word or line selection's bounds from ghostty_text_s instead of re-driving clicks
